# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17 (Bi-Vb Pc17)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc17  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17  
**Title (English, from literature):** Putting out bedding without permission  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17 (known as *Anāpucchāsantharaṇa*, "Putting out bedding without permission") is a monastic disciplinary rule belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule proscribes a nun from spreading out bedding in a house and then sitting or lying down on it without first requesting permission from the owners, an offense entailing expiation (*pācittiya*). As noted by Ute Hüsken, this training rule forms part of a thematic sequence alongside Bhikkhunī Pācittiyas 15 and 16 addressing conduct when visiting lay households in the afternoon (*pacchābhattaṁ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā*), specifically curbing overly familiar behavior and violations of guest etiquette [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Parallels exist in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda (in both Chinese and Tibetan versions), Mahāsāṅghika, and the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda Vinaya.
